quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This position lets experienced riders at the back watch over them.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from road edges, and ride in tire tracks made by other cars.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Allow the other driver to pass you.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If safe, change lanes and let them go ahead. Speeding up only increases danger and encourages more tailgating.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible while riding?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on all the time. Wear bright and reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed for safety.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel skids while braking?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake right away and re-apply it smoothly.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support your body. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle begins to wobble?

options.text: Accelerate out of the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate—it makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, gradually slow down by closing the throttle, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no defects.
Looks attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: When securing a load on a motorcycle, place it:

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and centered. Placing them high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off balance. Distribute the load evenly on both sides of the motorcycle to prevent it from pulling to one side.

questions.question: Which one is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, full-fingered gloves, and heavy denim pants protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right, you should usually:

options.text: Stay on the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Not worry about the parked cars.
Look at the left edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride toward the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This keeps you away from opening doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to adjust your position for changing conditions.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not use your headlight.
Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Always use your headlight.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either one.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow other vehicles as closely as possible.
Focus only on your controls and not look ahead.
Show other drivers your intentions with signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers your intentions with signals.
questions.explanation: Make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The center of the lane usually has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from vehicles builds up in the center of lanes. In dry conditions, this strip usually has enough traction for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center part of the lane. Avoid it when roads are wet.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully extended.
Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid hazards on the road surface.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: How long can marijuana's effects last?

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana affects you within minutes and effects last 2 to 4 hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Use extra space if your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Increase your distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: The claim that a motorcycle helmet limits side vision is:

options.text: True. Vision is limited and can be unsafe.
True, but only on sunny days.
True. Side vision is limited.
False. Vision is not limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: False. Vision is not limited.
questions.explanation: An approved motorcycle helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
